Subject: Request: detailed perf methodology and observed metrics for model serving

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Procurement and our SRE leads asked for a more concrete deliverable to include with our RFP response: a reproducible performance validation runbook that lays out test harness, traffic profiles, expected p50/p95/p99 numbers for a typical LLM conversation workload, warmup strategy, and scaling behavior (both autoscale and manual reserved capacity).

Can you share:
- A test matrix (concurrency, sequence lengths, prompt shapes) you recommend we run
- Baseline p50/p95/p99 for a 7B and 30B open model variant under both hosted and dedicated configurations
- How Redwood handles queueing, batching, and prefix cache effects on tail latency
- Any artifacts we can use to reproduce results (scripts, environment specs)

We're hoping to include a Redwood-authored runbook and sample results in our RFP appendix by EOD 2026-12-06. If you can provide a joint-run proposal and any attachments today or tomorrow that would be ideal.

Thanks,
Emma
Emma Lewis

Globex Corporation

From: karthik_iyer 
To: Emma Lewis <emma.lewis@globex.com>
Cc: marissa_cole, ben_carter, Procurement <procurement@globex.com>

Subject: Re: Request: detailed perf methodology and observed metrics for model serving

Emma —

Appreciate the clear ask. I pulled together a draft runbook and a small set of representative results from our lab runs. Attaching: redwood-perf-runbook-v1.pdf (test plan + scripts), globex-joint-run-matrix.xlsx (recommended matrix), and a short CSV with summary stats from a 6-hour run on our Dedicated pool. High level summary below, full details in the attachments.

High level (short):
- Test harness: k6-based synthetic driver + our replay wrapper to preserve tokenization and streaming semantics; metrics exported to Prometheus and aggregated with histogram buckets for latency.
- Configs tested: hosted-small (shared GPUs, standard throttles) and dedicated-12g (3x A100-style GPU nodes, per-tenant pool).
- Models: open-7B-quant (int8-friendly) and opt-30B-qat (float16).
- Representative p50/p95/p99 (mixed-conversation workload, seq len distribution 8/32/128 tokens):
  - 7B hosted-small: p50 28ms, p95 125ms, p99 410ms (tokens/sec 1,800 at steady-state, batching ON)
  - 7B dedicated-12g: p50 14ms, p95 68ms, p99 190ms (tokens/sec 4,600)
  - 30B dedicated-12g: p50 42ms, p95 210ms, p99 620ms (tokens/sec 1,700)
- Tail behavior: p99 driven primarily by cold KV-cache misses and bursty concurrency; enabling prefix caching and an initial warmup wave reduces p99 by ~35%.

Key notes and reproducibility:
- Warmup: recommend a 10–15 minute progressive warmup (ramp from 5% to target QPS). This primes KV caches and keeps kernels JIT-warmed on dedicated hardware.
- Batching: our runtime continuously forms context-aware micro-batches; target batch sizes and max latency thresholds are tunable. The runbook includes example batch configs used to generate the attached CSV.
- Autoscale behavior: in Dedicated we scale by adding nodes when sustained GPU utilization > 70% for 90s; burst capacity configured to allow short spikes (up to 2x) for 2 minutes before backpressure rejects. The runbook documents knob values and test scripts to exercise scaling.
- Observability: we emit per-request traces, token-level timing, and queue depth histograms to Prometheus. Dashboard links and sample alert thresholds are in the runbook.

I'll coordinate with Marissa for a brief joint-run next week if you'd like us to execute the matrix against Globex staging. If you want faster numbers we can prioritize the 7B runs first.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-perf-runbook-v1.pdf; globex-joint-run-matrix.xlsx; run-results-summary-20261201.csv

Thanks Karthik — this is helpful. A couple clarifying items from our SRE review:

1) For the p99 numbers you quoted, can you confirm the exact request/response size? Are those per-token latencies or end-to-end for a response with 64 generated tokens?
2) For autoscale: if you scale from N to N+1 nodes, what's the observed latency bump during that window (we are sensitive to mid-run node joins)?
3) Could you expose the test harness code or a Docker image so our SREs can run the same driver within our staging network (we cannot allow outbound test traffic to Redwood labs)?

Also — procurement wants the explicit acceptance criteria we use to mark a test run as successful vs inconclusive. Could you include that in the runbook?

Emma

Subject: Re: Request: detailed perf methodology and observed metrics for model serving

Emma —

Answering your bullets:

1) Latency semantics: the quoted p50/p95/p99 are end-to-end server-side request latencies measured from request receive to last-token-served at the server, aggregated on a per-response basis. For the CSV we've included a breakdown: connection+queuing time, first-token time, and per-token increment. The sample numbers I referenced used responses with an average of 64 generated tokens and variable prompt sizes (prompt avg ~40 tokens). We'll add explicit example rows to the CSV.

2) Node join impact: when scaling up we stream model weights to the new node; during the short window where load shifts there's a modest p95 bump — observed median increase in p95 of ~1.2–1.6x for 30–90s depending on model size. We mitigate by: 1) pre-warming replicas when possible; 2) using small-step scaling (one node at a time); 3) routing new requests preferentially to warmed nodes. Values in the runbook simulate both pre-warm and cold-join scenarios.

3) Test harness availability: yes — we built a dockerized harness (k6 + replay wrapper + prometheus exporter). We can't provide outbound access to Redwood labs, but we can provide the image and a launch script that runs entirely inside Globex staging. See drive link in our attachments. We'll add an explicit section on how to run offline and how to map your staging GPU nodes to our test matrix.

Acceptance criteria (short):
- Run stability: no sustained GPU OOMs; throughput within ±10% of expected for the steady-state window; no error rate > 0.5% for 5-minute windows.
- Latency SLOs: p95 within target bound per model conf (documented in runbook); p99 must not exceed 2x target without documented root cause.
- Regression checks: compare to baseline run; regressions > 8% on p95 or >12% on tokens/sec flagged as inconclusive and require deeper analysis.

If that works, we can produce an amended runbook today with these clarifications and a short-run on your staging next week. Ben — can you drop the docker image tag and confirm the run matrix perms for Globex?

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Principal Performance Architect, Redwood Inference
